content_preview.title: Rackspace Spot Breach Let Attackers Read Customer Kubernetes Secrets Using Leaked Credentials, Rackspace Says
content_preview.summary: Rackspace says attackers used leaked credentials to access its Spot Kubernetes platform on November 17, reading customer Secrets and deploying unauthorized pods.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Rackspace has told customers that an unauthorized party used leaked credentials to break into its Rackspace Spot cloud platform, gaining access to Kubernetes Secrets stored in affected customer clusters, according to [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/rackspace-spot-breach-let-hackers-access-customer-kubernetes-secrets/), which obtained the customer notification. Rackspace Spot is a cloud platform that lets organizations deploy and manage containerized...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean News-category writeup of a single breach notification report: Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure, neutral incident-report tone, no sensationalism or editorializing. 604 words, within the 400-1200 News range.
editor_notes.source_verification: 2 sources, both read in full from the committed snapshots (not re-fetched). source-0.html.gz (BleepingComputer, 'Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets' by Lawrence Abrams, Nov 21 2026) was fetched via Archive.org fallback per manifest.json (archive_fallback: true, original returned 200 but the bot-check heuristic routed to the Wayback capture anyway) -- decompressed and sha256-verified (665be367...e02a1ee matches manifest) before reading; the extracted text confirms it is the genuine BleepingComputer article (Wayback banner + byline + full body present), not a block/placeholder page. source-1.html.gz (kubernetes.io Secrets docs) fetched live (sha256 a657317c...7b1673 verified). Every claim in the article traces to one of these two sources; no orphan body URLs (both cited URLs appear in article.sources and in body_markdown, confirmed by the script's 'sources_referenced'/'body_sources_match' checks). No suspicious_patterns flagged in manifest.json for either source; none found on manual read either. Anthropic disclosure: not required - no mention of Anthropic, Claude, or an Anthropic-operated product anywhere in the article.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Quote-by-quote audit against the raw BleepingComputer snapshot text: (1) Rackspace notification excerpt -- article renders 'On 17 November 2026 (about 00:20-22:00 UTC), an unauthorized party used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot.' verbatim against the source's identical quoted sentence ('"On 17 November 2026 (about 00:20-22:00 UTC), an unauthorized party used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot," reads the notification.') -- exact match, including the en-dash and UTC range. (2) Sirish Raghuram/Platform9 quote -- article's two quoted sentences ('I've been instrumental in creating Spot...let you down in this way' and 'I know you disagree...best protect everyone using Spot.') match the source's two consecutive quoted sentences verbatim, word-for-word; the article's 'adding:' connector is an editorial seam joining two separately-quoted source sentences, not an alteration of either quote's wording. Raghuram's title ('co-founder and Chief Growth Officer of Platform9, which co-developed Rackspace Spot with Rackspace') matches the source exactly. Timeline verified against source: intrusion Nov 17 ~00:20-22:00 UTC (source: 'attackers accessed parts of the platform on November 17, 2026, between approximately 00:20 and 22:00 UTC' -- matches), discovery Nov 18 via customer report (source: 'Rackspace says it learned of the intrusion on November 18 after receiving a customer report and confirmed that the recipient's organization was affected that same day' -- matches; article's 'reporting customer's organization' is a faithful paraphrase of 'recipient's organization,' not a quote), full restoration Nov 21 (source: 'Rackspace announced that service had been fully restored on November 21' -- exact match). IOCs (IP 23.224.79.106, range 23.224.0.0/15, prefixes i1/glm-/probe) match the source's indicator list exactly. Unknown-figures check: article's 'What We Don't Know' states 'Rackspace has not disclosed how many customers were affected' and that BleepingComputer 'asked Rackspace both how many customers were affected and whether customer data was stolen, but had not received a response' -- this matches the source's 'BleepingComputer contacted Rackspace to ask how many customers were affected and whether customer data was stolen, but has not received a response' precisely. The article invents no customer count or confirmed-data-theft figure anywhere; both are correctly left as unknown/unconfirmed in both headline/summary and body. The Kubernetes Secret definition quote ('is an object that contains a small amount of sensitive data such as a password, a token, or a key') is verbatim from kubernetes.io's own docs page; the surrounding paraphrase about not needing to place such data 'directly in a Pod specification or container image' is a fair, non-quoted paraphrase of the source's 'Such information might otherwise be put in a Pod specification or in a container image' and is attributed, not quoted. Absence/quantifier claim-accuracy sweep (any/not disclosed/never/all) found 4 sentences; all are directly supported by the single BleepingComputer source text with no overreach beyond what it states.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral incident-report register throughout; attributions ('Rackspace says,' 'according to BleepingComputer,' 'BleepingComputer reports') are used consistently and nothing is stated as the Herald's own finding.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Rackspace or Rackspace Spot coverage found in src/content/articles/ (grep -ril 'rackspace' returned nothing). Genuinely new topic, not a duplicate.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Single-source (plus a documentation citation) News breach report that is scrupulously accurate against the raw BleepingComputer text: both direct quotes verbatim, the full intrusion/discovery/restoration timeline confirmed, IOCs confirmed, and the 'customer count and data-theft status unknown' framing is itself verified rather than papered over with an invented number. No corrections needed. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurately sourced breach report of interest to the cloud/Kubernetes security audience, but a single-incident report without broader industry analysis caps it below a 2.
